summary: KR-ZOOM-OUT-02's calibration-gate failure is independently re-diagnosed by a dedicated sensitivity demonstration as a generator-parameterisation problem (three inert/weak parameters used, three genuinely sensitive parameters found instead); a self-caught silent softening of the frozen grid-adequacy criterion is flagged, deliberated, and resolved as a formal amendment (operational gate-reachability replacing the literal span-width rule, with an anti-permissiveness clause); KR-ZOOM-OUT-03 is then frozen, its calibration gate is met on a fresh seed, a known precision limitation is recorded before execution rather than explained after, and execution is authorized with the explicit caveat that passing the gate is not evidence for the hypothesis.
contribution_assessment: A further installment of the same rigorous pre-registration/calibration discipline seen across S2809-S2811, distinguished by two further self-caught process failures (a silently softened frozen criterion, and an overclaimed diagnosis) each corrected via explicit, recorded amendment rather than silent repair, and by treating a discovered statistical-power limitation as a fact to declare rather than a problem to fix by adjusting the protocol.

summary: Synthesizes the whole Zoom-in/Zoom-out experiment series (KR-ZOOM-01/02, KR-ZOOM-OUT-01/02/03) into an operational-vs-proven-primitive distinction (Zoom-in is operationally usable as an engineering pattern; Zoom-out remains undefined and usable only as a workflow hypothesis), then proposes and elaborates a Knowledge-Graph architectural hypothesis in which Zoom-out is reframed not as an inverse of Zoom-in but as a distinct Context Integration operation, explicitly separating the graph representational substrate from KnowledgeOS's epistemic mechanics, and recommends a new KR-CONTEXT-INTEGRATION-01 experiment in place of further symmetric Zoom-out tests.
contribution_assessment: A synthesis and reframing document that treats the entire preceding experiment series (S2807-S2812) as settled evidence to build on, explicitly refusing to retroactively reinterpret null/degenerate Zoom-out results as support for the newly proposed Context Integration hypothesis. All architectural proposals are explicitly labelled [PROP]/research hypothesis, not Theory v1.2 or kernel law.

summary: Refines the Knowledge Graph / KnowledgeOS separation into a three-layer architecture (representation, epistemic computation, execution/governance), argues a bare graph cannot answer ten KnowledgeOS-specific questions, evaluates Vera Birkenbihl's 'Stroh im Kopf?' as an inspirational (not architectural) source for knowledge-as-network ideas relevant to Zoom-in/Zoom-out, and states a general methodological principle that external metaphors from any tradition (Vedic, Birkenbihl, Dretske, etc.) may inspire but never dictate KnowledgeOS architecture.
contribution_assessment: Continues directly from S2813's Knowledge Graph hypothesis, sharpening it into an explicit three-layer architecture, then applies the established external-source discipline (already seen with the Gita strand in S2805/S2807) to a new source (Birkenbihl), extracting specific structural analogies while explicitly refusing to let them dictate kernel primitives. All book-derived claims are extracted as this document's own interpretive commentary, not KnowledgeOS facts.

summary: Surveys and ranks six candidate books as metaphorical (not architectural) lenses for KnowledgeOS -- Way's Knowledge Representation and Metaphor, Pearl & Mackenzie's The Book of Why, Birkenbihl's Stroh im Kopf?, Hofstadter's I Am a Strange Loop, Gleick's The Information, and Calvino's Invisible Cities -- each mapped to a specific KnowledgeOS distinction or open question, explicitly rejecting a unified 'KnowledgeOS books canon' in favor of an Inspirational Metaphor Corpus with a fixed Metaphor->Question->Hypothesis->Experiment pipeline.
contribution_assessment: A survey document applying the inspiration-not-specification discipline established in S2814 to a broader set of candidate external sources, each explicitly scoped to a specific KnowledgeOS question rather than treated as authoritative. All book-derived claims are this document's own interpretive mapping, not KnowledgeOS facts.

summary: Evaluates Maxwell Maltz's Psycho-Cybernetics as an inspirational (not epistemological) metaphor for KnowledgeOS's goal/feedback/correction/action dynamics, mapping its servo-mechanism vocabulary onto the existing K_t/I_t/Delta_t/Theta structure, explicitly separating cybernetic error from KnowledgeOS Zero, keeping the controller-vs-mechanism kernel question open, and closing with a reviewer's tightening that rejects assuming monotonic epistemic convergence and introduces an oscillation-vs-revision distinction and a candidate (undefined) epistemic-stability function.
contribution_assessment: Continues the same inspiration-not-specification discipline applied to the Gita and Birkenbihl strands (S2805/S2807/S2814), extracting a cybernetic goal-feedback-correction metaphor while explicitly refusing to import unsupported psychological claims or assume convergence properties the corpus's own prior findings already contradict. All claims are extracted as this document's own interpretive commentary on the book, not KnowledgeOS facts.

summary: Formalizes a strict cybernetics-to-epistemics lexicon (rejecting naive term equivalences like Error=Zero and Convergence=Determination), reframes cybernetics from a dynamics metaphor into an independent kernel-discovery lens generating candidate capabilities (State, Reference, Compare, Detect Deviation, Select Correction, Transform State, Feedback) that must each pass a capability-simulation/irreducibility test rather than being assumed primitive, finds Feedback is derivable (not irreducible) under the tested contract, keeps Select Correction's kernel-vs-environment placement explicitly open, and ends by strengthening a promotion rule from a false IFF into a necessary-but-not-sufficient admissibility gate, with a final invariant that convergence of multiple independent metaphors never by itself establishes kernel necessity.
contribution_assessment: The most rigorous and iterative installment of the cybernetics-as-metaphor strand (continuing S2816), turning a loose dynamics analogy into a disciplined kernel-discovery methodology through repeated self-correction (rejecting an IFF promotion rule, rejecting multi-lens agreement as a membership criterion, keeping one capability's placement genuinely open rather than letting the metaphor decide). All cybernetic mappings and capability-derivability claims are extracted as this document's own analytical proposals, not established KnowledgeOS facts; Theory v1.2 and the kernel baseline are stated unchanged throughout.

summary: Proposes animal/biological communication (vervet alarm calls, signalling games, honesty/deception, cue-vs-signal, honeybee dances, quorum sensing) as a new [EXT][RESEARCH LENS] for KnowledgeOS's Observation->Signal->Information->Assessment->Action transition, extracting candidate communication-algebra operations (Encode, Interpret, Combine, Corroborate, Contradict, Update) and receiver-relativity/deception/actionable-information distinctions that echo existing KnowledgeOS separations, then self-corrects by separating commutativity (a mathematical property) from evidence independence (a generative-process property) and mandating pure structural extraction across five biological systems before any cross-system algebra is hypothesized.
contribution_assessment: Applies the established inspiration-not-specification discipline (Gita, Birkenbihl, Maltz) to a new external lens, biological communication, with an unusually productive yield of candidate formal distinctions that echo (and are explicitly checked against) existing KnowledgeOS separations. Notable for a genuine methodological self-correction distinguishing mathematical operation properties from empirical evidence-generation properties. All biological claims and citations are extracted as this document's own research commentary, not established facts, and none are promoted beyond [PROP]/[OPEN] status.

summary: Extends the biological-communication lens (S2818) from one-shot alarm signals to multi-round reciprocal courtship communication, extracting a distributed bidirectional epistemic feedback loop (Signal!=Sender-State, Response->Evidence-not-Knowledge, Decision!=Belief), then develops a candidate 'communicative Zero Space' distinguishing non-response/rejection/challenge from a formal Zero verdict, proposes and then self-corrects an exploratory KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01 protocol (removing pre-assigned Zero classifications and an assumed hypothesis-space-expansion direction), adds a mandatory non-communication control, and finally grounds the whole biological metaphor in two concrete distributed-systems test cases (HTTP timeout, database lock contention).
contribution_assessment: A very long, exploratory file with substantial internal duplication: the 'Yes -- this is a much sharper way to use the biological example' passage (roughly lines 595-1086) is repeated near-verbatim starting at line 1088. Extracted once here. The file culminates in a genuine self-correction cycle (removing pre-assigned Zero labels and an assumed hypothesis-space-direction from its own initial protocol) and in translating the biological metaphor into concrete, testable distributed-systems scenarios -- a notable move from pure analogy toward an implementable experiment design. All biological and Zero-space claims are extracted as this document's own research proposals, explicitly held at [EXT]/[PROP]/[OPEN]/[DESIGN] status with Theory v1.2 and the kernel untouched throughout.

in_file_overlap_claim.target: The section beginning 'Yes -- this is a much sharper way to use the biological example' (covering non-response!=Zero, the candidate Zero Space concept, challenge vs rejection, actionable-vs-epistemic closure, the formal communication-Zero definition, the distinct communication states, Zero-of-the-relationship, and the initial KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01 proposal) is repeated near-verbatim a second time later in the same file.

summary: Finalizes the KR-BIOCOMM-ZERO-01 protocol through several rounds of tightening: separates biological source from software analogue into an explicit four-layer pipeline with the rule that external observation never jumps directly to a KnowledgeOS claim (B does not imply KOS), corrects a mis-scoped preservation contract and an over-weak O-F* degeneracy check (learning directly from the KR-ZOOM-OUT-03 failure), rewrites an implicational hypothesis into two neutral frequency estimands, and proposes replacing a single binary Zero value with a richer per-contract preservation signature, closing with the explicit target question of whether KnowledgeOS Zero is compositional or requires relational information.
contribution_assessment: The concluding installment of the biological-communication/Zero-space strand (S2818-S2820), notable for explicitly generalizing its own discipline into a reusable multi-lens methodology (stated to also govern how the Vedic material should be used) and for two corrections that directly reuse lessons already learned earlier in the same overall research programme (the O-F* degeneracy-check weakness, diagnosed identically in the KR-ZOOM-OUT-03 thread). All formalizations remain explicitly [PROP]/[OPEN]/[DESIGN], with Theory v1.2 and the kernel stated frozen/untouched throughout.
